correctness.rationale: For every W1,1 driver, the terminal output equals signed area. Doubling the open curve by reflected reversed traversal gives signed area 2F and length at most 2B; the signed isoperimetric inequality proves the bound. A deterministic adversary leaves one nonempty unqueried transition gap for any finite query sequence, even when times are not ordered. The two length-B semicircle completions produce identical transcript and outputs of opposite magnitude B^2/(2pi). Sympy integration was checked for the exact arc identity, not substituted for the infinite-policy proof. All quantifiers and boundary N=1 are covered.

value.rationale: A global path-length budget is a natural alternative regularity model in controlled ODE and rough-path analysis. The sharp constant B^2/(2pi) for every finite observation budget exhibits an exact non-decaying information regime, unlike the source paper’s N^{-1} pointwise-speed regime. The explicit adversarial strategy explains why adaptive point sampling fails; this answers a substantive sampling-regularity boundary question rather than an arbitrary specialization or merely numerical computation.
